title: introduce-stream-checkpointing-and-retry-presets-across-py-ts-go
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Provide a small, consistent ergonomics improvement across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs that makes long-lived streaming sessions more resilient and easier to integrate with application-level checkpointing. This PR introduces a lightweight stream checkpointing API (checkpoint/restore points for pull/push streams) plus a curated set of Retry Presets (backoff profiles) that teams can opt into. The goal is parity across SDKs for the most common production patterns (resuming partially-read streams and applying well-tested backoff profiles) without forcing teams to adopt a monolithic session manager.

Summary of changes: added StreamCheckpoint API to each SDK (py: StreamCheckpoint class + helper methods, ts: StreamCheckpoint interface + resume helpers, go: streamcheckpoint package + examples); introduced RetryPreset enum/config with three profiles (fast, balanced, conservative) implemented in each SDK and wired into existing retry machinery; bumped SDK package versions (py 3.1.0 -> 3.2.0, ts 2.7.0 -> 2.8.0, go 1.9.0 -> 1.10.0) and updated changelogs.

Compatibility notes: default behaviors are unchanged unless the new APIs are used. RetryPresets are additive wrappers around existing retry config - existing users using custom backoff or the old retry config will not be affected. StreamCheckpoint is opt-in: callers must explicitly create a checkpoint handle and pass it when rehydrating a consumer.

Testing: unit tests added for all SDKs (stream resume semantics, checkpoint integrity, and preset mapping). Integration smoke tests validate a resume after simulated network interruption and ensure token reauth is preserved across resume when session is sticky. Added CI matrix rows for python/ts/go examples.

Migration/mode of operation: doc snippets added to each SDK README showing a minimal resume flow. Example flow: start stream, persist checkpoint token/id, on reconnect instantiate consumer with restore_from(checkpoint). For teams who rely on session affinity, this integrates with the existing session lease logic and does not change lease semantics.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged on the server for a small subset of customers for initial telemetry; SDK APIs are available immediately and gated by a transparent opt-in. If there are regressions we will cut a patch and revert the client-side usage only (no server break).

Checklist: [x] Design review (ENG-1428), [x] Unit tests added, [x] Integration smoke tests, [x] Docs/README snippets, [x] Version bumps and changelog entries, [x] CI green

Related: ENG-1428 (stream resiliency initiative), ENG-1501 (sdk ergonomics sprint), SUP-859 (customer support follow-up for stream resume incidents).

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Can we get an explicit note on how this interacts with token rotation? Specifically: does restoring a checkpoint replay old token windows? (author reply: checkpoint stores a session-ref but not raw credentials; restore will trigger normal token refresh hooks so tokens are not replayed)
Lucia Gomez: The Go restore path had a data race in CI; I left a suggested mutex-based patch. (author reply: applied suggested mutex and added a targeted unit test to cover concurrent restores)
Ethan Park: Suggest add a small example for a serverless resume pattern in TS. (author reply: added serverless example and included it in the matrix)
Ops-bot: ci/integration-smoke failed on first run due to flaky network; reran and passed.
release_notes: SDKs: added opt-in StreamCheckpoint API that enables application-level stream resume semantics; added RetryPreset profiles (fast, balanced, conservative) to simplify backoff choices; bumped SDK versions (py 3.2.0, ts 2.8.0, go 1.10.0). No breaking changes by default.
notes_for_backport: No server-side dependency required. Backport only if customers request immediate patch in older minor versions; backport steps: cherry-pick checkpoint API and preset config files and regenerate changelog.
testing_instructions: Run unit tests per SDK (make test-python, npm test in typescript, go test ./...); run integration smoke matrix (ci/matrix/sdk-tri-checkpoint.yml) which simulates network blips and validates resume token semantics.
additional_context: This PR is intended to be a small cross-SDK ergonomic win rather than a full session-manager overhaul. We avoided centralizing session state to reduce server coupling and to keep the client surface small.
example_usage_snippet:
python:
from redwood_sdk.streaming import StreamCheckpoint, StreamConsumer
cp = StreamCheckpoint.capture(consumer)
# persist cp.id to DB
# later
consumer = StreamConsumer.restore_from(cp.id)
# consumer resumes from last acknowledged chunk
